item.title: Federal Watchdog Investigates Adam Kinzinger for Kalshi Bets on His Pardon
item.description: The inquiry by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission centers on bets the former congressman made on Kalshi in the weeks before he was pardoned in January 2025.
item.dc:creator: Sharon LaFraniere
item.media:credit: Eric Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: Former Representative Adam Kinzinger was a member of the House select committee that investigated the January 2021 attack on the Capitol.

item.title: Taking On Trump Immigration Agenda, Justices Will Review Migrant Detention Policy
item.description: The administration’s policy of detaining immigrants who crossed the border illegally years ago and holding them without a bond hearing has divided lower courts.
item.dc:creator: Ann E. Marimow
item.media:credit: Tierney L. Cross for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Supreme Court will be considering the legality of some of the most controversial aspects of the Trump administration’s efforts to rapidly expel millions of migrants living in the United States.

item.title: Renewable Energy Super PAC Targets 7 Republicans With $15 Million War Chest
item.description: Most of the Republicans, such as Lauren Boebert of Colorado and Victoria Spartz of Indiana, are incumbents in districts that President Trump won comfortably in 2024.
item.dc:creator: Reid J. Epstein
item.media:credit: Al Drago for The New York Times
item.media:description: Representative Lauren Boebert, Republican of Colorado, is one of seven congressional Republicans being targeted by a super PAC backed by renewable energy investors.

item.title: Oil Is Flowing From the Persian Gulf, but Prices Remain High. Why?
item.description: Crude oil costs close to $100 a barrel because traders are worried hostilities could soon restart and the world is burning through its emergency stockpiles.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca F. Elliott
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Ruth Fremson/The New York Times
item.media:description: Governments and companies the world over have been draining their oil storage tanks over the past seven months to keep a lid on prices.

item.title: Texas Governor Race Puts Pressure on Andy Beshear and Democratic Governors Association
item.description: Allies of Gina Hinojosa want a Democratic group to support her bid for Texas governor — putting pressure on its chairman, Gov. Andy Beshear of Kentucky, who is weighing a run for president.
item.dc:creator: Reid J. Epstein
item.media:credit: Christopher Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: Gina Hinojosa is the Democratic candidate running for governor of Texas against the incumbent, Gov. Greg Abbott.

item.title: John Roberts Retreated to His Island. Supreme Court Critics Found Him.
item.description: After decades of potlucks and paddle-boarding on Maine’s midcoast, rising anger and protests have left the Supreme Court’s chief justice more isolated than ever.
item.dc:creator: Jodi Kantor
item.media:credit: Ryan David Brown for The New York Times

item.title: In Wooing Wavering Hispanic Voters, Trump Talks ICE, His Ballroom and Himself
item.description: President Trump veered off the topic at hand during a White House reception for Hispanic Heritage Month.
item.dc:creator: Erica L. Green
item.media:credit: Doug Mills/The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump’s remarks offered a glimpse into how his attempts to help his party in the midterms often clash with his brand of personality-driven politics.

item.title: Federal Judge Orders Bureau of Prisons to Restore Union Protections
item.description: In his ruling, Judge Vernon D. Oliver cited public statements from the bureau’s director that hurt the agency’s case in court.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.media:credit: Luke Sharrett for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Bureau of Prisons had argued in court it was merely carrying out an executive order from President Trump instructing a broad swath of government agencies to end collective bargaining with federal unions.

item.title: Senator Marsha Blackburn Sues Over Jack Smith’s Subpoena During Trump Inquiry
item.description: The lawsuit, brought by Senator Marsha Blackburn of Tennessee, tests the reach of the Constitution’s “speech or debate” clause.

item.category: House Select Committee to Investigate the January 6th Attack
item.media:credit: Photographs by Kenny Holston/The New York Times
item.media:description: Senator Marsha Blackburn’s lawsuit seeks a declaration that Jack Smith, the former special counsel, conspired to violate her rights during an investigation into Donald J. Trump.

item.title: OpenAI’s Greg Brockman Backs Out of Second $25 Million Donation to A.I. Super PAC
item.description: Greg Brockman, OpenAI’s president and co-founder, said internally that the super PAC, Leading the Future, had become a “distraction” for the A.I. company.

item.title: Trump’s Voluntary A.I. Policing Echoes What Biden Did. But Is It Enough Today?
item.description: President Trump’s plan to let A.I. companies police themselves comes amid mounting examples that they are failing to put safeguards on the technology.
item.dc:creator: David E. Sanger
item.media:credit: Doug Mills/The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump embraces Elon Musk while standing with other tech leaders outside the White House on Tuesday.

item.title: Justice Dept. Tries to Rebuke Federal Judges for Speaking to The Times
item.description: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz had warned that the administration’s actions “created a grave threat to the rule of law.” The attorney general accused him of “obvious bias.”
item.dc:creator: Mattathias Schwartz and Devlin Barrett
item.media:credit: Jenn Ackerman for The New York Times
item.media:description: Judge Patrick Schiltz said he was “acting well within the ethical rules that apply to federal judges in speaking to The New York Times.”

item.title: No More Drugstore Head Shots: Passport Applications Go Digital
item.description: The process of getting a first U.S. passport will go fully online next year, said Secretary of State Marco Rubio, so if your picture is bad, it’ll be your fault.
item.dc:creator: Gabe Castro-Root
item.media:credit: Eric Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: The State Department, which last summer issued a limited number of “patriot passports” with President Trump’s image, is making broader design changes to all passports in 2028, including “more gold” on the cover.

item.title: Legal Immigrants Lose Medicaid Coverage Under Trump’s Bill
item.description: Many immigrants without green cards will no longer be eligible for the health insurance program for low-income people.
item.dc:creator: Madeleine Ngo
item.media:credit: Maddie McGarvey for The New York Times
item.media:description: Farahzad Sediqi is set to lose Medicaid, which helps cover her treatment for multiple sclerosis, a disorder of the central nervous system that can cause paralysis and seizures.

item.title: Democrats Block Stock-Trading Bill, Denying the G.O.P. a Pre-Midterm Win
item.description: A Republican measure to limit, but not bar, congressional stock trading faltered in the Senate as Democrats thwarted a G.O.P. bid to show progress on an issue that has rankled voters.
item.dc:creator: Annie Karni
item.media:credit: Karsten Moran for The New York Times
item.media:description: Stock trading by members of Congress has become a politically toxic issue for both parties, one that they are trying to use against each other in competitive midterm races.

item.title: Congress Set to Leave Washington for the Midterms With No A.I. Progress
item.description: Senate Democrats blocked a measure that would encourage, but not require, states to protect consumers from power rate hikes tied to data center growth, and had no limits on A.I. use or deployment.
item.dc:creator: Michael Gold and Cecilia Kang
item.media:credit: Paul Ratje for The New York Times
item.media:description: New homes encircle a park at Vista Del Norte Estates as construction progresses on the Meta artificial intelligence data center being built in northeast El Paso, Texas in July.

item.title: E.E.O.C. Sues Harvard for Data on Diversity in Hiring Practices
item.description: The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission filed a lawsuit asking a judge to compel the university to provide information on hiring practices that the agency said discriminated against white men.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Davis O’Brien and Michael C. Bender
item.media:credit: Sophie Park for The New York Times
item.media:description: Harvard has been a frequent target of federal officials under the Trump administration.

item.title: Calder Sculpture ‘Mountains and Clouds’ Is Restored in Senate Office
item.description: The effort to reunite two halves of Alexander Calder’s monumental “Mountains and Clouds” hit many snags, until donors and legislators from both parties stepped in.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Diaz
item.media:credit: Calder Foundation, New York/Artists Rights Society (ARS), New York; Photograph by Caroline Gutman for The New York Times
item.media:description: The crew watches as a cloud is hoisted into place above Calder’s mountains in the Hart Senate Office Building. Later a motor will be installed to try to make the clouds move as Calder intended.
